bindings.label: A 47-year-old woman presented for evaluation of a cardiac murmur without displaying any cardiac symptoms

Heart murmur had been detected at age 3; she had no daily physical restriction except in physical education class, gave birth to two children at ages 26 and 27 without complications, and had no family history of cardiac conditions
The patient noticed her fingers and shoe size getting bigger in her early 30s and experienced menopause at 35 years of age; thickening of all fingers, lips, and nose was observed

Physical examination: height 154.6 cm, weight 63.3 kg (BMI 26.5 kg/m²), blood pressure 106/56 mm Hg, heart rate 68 beats/min, cardiac exam revealed a 4/6 systolic ejection murmur at the second to third left sternal border
Echocardiography shows a quadricuspid aortic valve with four equal cusps and spherical morphology
Echocardiography shows severe outflow obstruction with peak gradient 131.1 mm Hg
Echocardiography shows severe left ventricular hypertrophy and apical aneurysm
Quadricuspid aortic valve causing severe outflow obstruction
Acromegaly contributes to left ventricular hypertrophy as a secondary modifying condition
Left ventricular apical aneurysm is a complication of severe quadricuspid aortic valve outflow obstruction
